the interrogations mishnah (Sanhedrin 40a), cited תנן התם

props.gloss_en: R' Meir: chametz may be eaten through the entire fifth hour
R' Yehuda: chametz may be eaten only through the entire fourth hour
R' Yehuda: during the fifth hour one suspends -- neither eating nor burning
chametz is burned at the start of the sixth hour -- it may be kept only until then
R' Yehuda: two invalid toda loaves lay on the bench as the public marker -- both present: all eat; one removed: all suspend; both removed: all burn
Rabban Gamliel: unconsecrated chametz is eaten through the fourth hour only
Rabban Gamliel: teruma is eaten through the fifth hour, and burning is at the start of the sixth
witnesses differing by one day of the month: testimony stands -- one knows of the month's intercalation and one does not
witnesses differing by two days of the month: testimony void
one says the second hour and one says the third: testimony stands
one says the third hour and one the fifth: testimony void -- R' Meir
one says the third hour and one the fifth: testimony stands -- R' Yehuda
one says the fifth hour and one the seventh: void for all -- at five the sun is in the east, at seven in the west
at the fifth hour the sun is in the east and at the seventh in the west -- no one errs across that divide
(Abaye, version 1) on R' Meir's view a person errs not at all: the event sat on the two/three boundary, one witness naming the end of the second hour and one the start of the third
(Abaye, version 1) on R' Yehuda's view a person errs half an hour: the event at the mid-point, each witness off by half an hour toward his own report
(Abaye, version 2) on R' Meir's view a person errs a trifle: the event was at the end of the second or the start of the third, and one of them errs a trifle
(Abaye, version 2) on R' Yehuda's view a person errs an hour and a trifle: the event at the end of the third or the start of the fifth, one witness off by an hour and a trifle
Rava: on R' Meir's view a person errs two hours less a trifle -- the event at the start of the second or the end of the third
Rava: on R' Yehuda's view a person errs three hours less a trifle -- the event at the start of the third or the end of the fifth
the seven interrogations mishnah: for a chakira (including 'which hour'), one witness's 'I do not know' voids the testimony
the chakirot matter because testimony must remain refutable by hazama; a 'don't know' would make it irrefutable
the answer: for hazama we credit the witnesses with their whole error-span, so the hour-interrogation remains refutable outside it
per R' Meir the credited span runs from the start of the first hour to the end of the fifth
per R' Yehuda the credited span runs from the start of the first hour to the end of the sixth
the span is not extended before sunrise: people do not confuse day with night
testimony is entrusted to the vigilant, who apply the full margin doctrine; chametz is entrusted to everyone, so the Sages drew its lines coarsely
Rav Adda bar Ahava: at six the sun stands at the meridian between east and west, so people DO err there
Rava rejects the zerizim answer as R' Yehuda's reason
the removal of chametz is only by burning
Rava's first account of R' Yehuda: the Sages assigned the fifth hour for gathering wood to burn the chametz
Ravina's baraita: R' Yehuda himself limits burning-only to before the hour of biur; at the hour of biur, hashbata is by any means
Rava's standing account of R' Yehuda: a decree on account of the cloudy day, when the sun's position cannot be read
Rav Pappa: the fourth hour is everyone's mealtime, so it is not confused with another hour even on a cloudy day
Rav Ashi: the Abaye/Rava dispute about testimony margins carries over unchanged to the chametz hours
and the point: the answers given above are real answers -- do not say the amoraim divide along tannaitic lines
